subject: math
title: Regular and Irregular Polygons: Name, Compare and Sort
seo_title: Grade 4 Math Regular and Irregular Polygons Worksheets (BC Curriculum, Free, Answer Key)
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 math worksheets on regular and irregular polygons for the BC curriculum: tell polygons from other shapes, name them by their sides, check for equal sides and equal angles, sort them in Venn diagrams and find polygons in real life. 100 questions with an answer key, good for FSA numeracy practice.
key_big: A regular polygon has all sides equal AND all angles equal. If not, it is irregular.
key_sub: A polygon is a closed shape with straight sides that do not cross. Name it by counting its sides. A rhombus has equal sides and a rectangle has equal angles, but neither is regular unless it is a square.
body_html:
What is a polygon?

A polygon is a flat, closed shape made of straight sides. The sides meet only at the corners, called vertices. A polygon can be any size, and it can be turned any way.

Name a polygon by its sides

Count the sides. A polygon has the same number of vertices as sides.

SidesNameRemember it
3triangletri = 3, like a tricycle
4quadrilateralquad = 4
5pentagonpenta = 5
6hexagona honeycomb cell
7heptagonhepta = 7
8octagonocto = 8, like an octopus; a stop sign
10decagondeca = 10
Example 1

A star has 5 points. What kind of polygon is it?

Do not count the points. Count the sides: each point has 2 sides, so 5 × 2 = 10.

Answer: a decagon

Regular or irregular?

A polygon is regular when all its sides are equal and all its angles are equal. If even one side or one angle is different, the polygon is irregular.

Marks help you check. Matching ticks show equal sides. A small square shows a right angle. Matching arcs show equal angles.

Example 2

Is a rhombus with 2 wide angles and 2 narrow angles regular?

Its 4 sides are equal. Its angles are not equal. A regular polygon needs both.

Answer: No, it is irregular

Sort polygons in a Venn diagram

A Venn diagram has two circles, each with a rule. A shape that fits both rules goes in the middle, where the circles overlap. A shape that fits neither rule goes outside both circles.

Example 3

The circles are “Regular” and “4 sides”. Where does a regular hexagon go?

It is regular, so it is in the “Regular” circle. It has 6 sides, not 4, so it is not in the other circle.

Answer: in “Regular” only

Polygons around you

A stop sign is a regular octagon. Honeycomb cells are regular hexagons. A yield sign is a regular triangle. A Canadian flag is a rectangle, so it is irregular. A hockey rink with rounded corners is not a polygon at all.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Calling a shape with a curve a polygonEvery side must be straight. One curve means it is not a polygon
Calling an open shape a polygonCheck that the shape is closed with no gaps
Equal sides means regularCheck the angles too. A rhombus has equal sides but is not regular
Equal angles means regularCheck the sides too. A rectangle has equal angles but is not regular
Missing a side or counting one twiceMark the vertex where you start and go around once
Naming a star by its pointsCount the sides. A 5-point star has 10 sides

faq.q: What is the difference between a regular and an irregular polygon?
faq.a: A regular polygon has all sides equal and all angles equal, like a square or a stop sign. If any side or angle is different, the polygon is irregular.

faq.q: Is a rhombus a regular polygon?
faq.a: Only when it is a square. A rhombus has 4 equal sides, but its angles are usually not equal, so most rhombuses are irregular.

faq.q: What do Grade 4 students learn about polygons in the BC curriculum?
faq.a: In Geometry and measurement, Grade 4 students learn regular and irregular polygons: they describe, name, compare and sort polygons by their sides and angles.

faq.q: How can I help my child practise polygons at home?
faq.a: Go on a shape hunt for signs, tiles and windows, count the sides together and ask whether all the sides and angles are equal. The 100 questions here also help with FSA numeracy practice.

items.q: Is this shape a polygon?
items.e: It is closed and has 5 straight sides. The sides do not need to be the same length.

items.q: Is this a polygon?
items.e: It is closed and every side is straight. The sides meet only at the corners, so it is a polygon.

items.q: Is this shape a polygon?
items.e: It is closed and it has 6 straight sides that meet only at the corners, so it is a polygon.

items.q: Is this shape a polygon?
items.e: The ends do not meet, so the shape is open. A polygon must be closed.
Three sides are straight, but the left side is curved. Every side of a polygon must be straight.
An oval is curved all the way around. A polygon has only straight sides.

items.q: Is this shape a polygon?
items.e: It is closed and has 3 straight sides. Every triangle is a polygon.
The bottom is straight, but the top is curved. A polygon has only straight sides.
C is made of two curved lines, so it is not a polygon. The other three are closed and have only straight sides.

items.q: Is this a polygon?
items.e: Two sides cross in the middle. In a polygon the sides meet only at the corners.

items.q: Is this shape a polygon?
items.e: The outline is 10 straight sides joined end to end. The sides do not cross, so the star is a polygon.

items.q: What is the smallest number of sides a polygon can have?
items.e: Two straight lines cannot close a shape. With 3 sides you get a triangle, the polygon with the fewest sides.

items.q: Is this a polygon?
items.e: It has 6 straight sides and it is closed. A polygon can have a corner that points in.

items.q: Is this shape a polygon?
items.e: The lines cross each other inside the shape. In a polygon the sides meet only at the corners and never cross.
B is closed and has 6 straight sides. The others have a curve, are open, or have sides that cross.
A circle is one curved line. It has no straight sides, so it is not a polygon.
The corners are curved. Even one curve means it is not a polygon.

items.q: Is this a polygon?
items.e: It is a square that has been turned. It is closed and has 4 straight sides, so it is a polygon. Turning a shape does not change that.

items.q: Is this a polygon?
items.e: There is a gap at the bottom, so the shape is not closed. A polygon must be closed.

items.q: A polygon is a closed shape made of …
items.e: A polygon is closed and all its sides are straight line segments. It can have 3 or more sides.

items.q: Which polygon has the most sides?
items.e: decagon 10, octagon 8, heptagon 7, hexagon 6. The decagon has the most.

items.q: What is the name of this polygon?
items.e: Mark the corner where you start, then count each side once: 8 sides. It is an octagon.

items.q: What is this polygon called?
items.e: It has 5 sides, so it is a pentagon.

items.q: How many vertices does a hexagon have?
items.e: A polygon has the same number of vertices (corners) as sides. A hexagon has 6 sides and 6 vertices.

items.q: What is this polygon called?
items.e: It has 8 sides, so it is an octagon. Octo means 8, like an octopus with 8 arms.

items.q: Ethan says, “A pentagon has 6 sides.” What is the mistake?
items.e: Penta means 5. A pentagon has 5 sides. A shape with 6 sides is a hexagon.

items.q: What is this polygon called?
items.e: Go around the outside and count: 6 sides. It is a hexagon, even though it does not look like a honeycomb cell.

items.q: Name this polygon.
items.e: Count every side, including the short ones beside the point: 7 sides. It is a heptagon.

items.q: Which shape is a heptagon?
items.e: D has 7 sides. The others have 6, 8 and 5 sides.

items.q: Emma counts the vertices of a polygon. There are 5. How many sides does it have?
items.e: Each side goes from one vertex to the next, so a polygon has as many sides as vertices: 5.

items.q: Name this polygon.
items.e: It has 10 sides, so it is a decagon. Deca means 10.

items.q: What is the name of this polygon?
items.e: It has 7 sides, so it is a heptagon.

items.q: Name this polygon.
items.e: It has 6 sides, so it is a hexagon.

items.q: What is the name of this polygon?
items.e: Count the sides around the outside: 2 roof sides, 2 walls and the bottom. That is 5 sides, so it is a pentagon.

items.q: Name this polygon.
items.e: It has 4 sides, so it is a quadrilateral. Its sides are all different, but it still has 4.

items.q: What is the name of this polygon?
items.e: It has 3 sides, so it is a triangle.

items.q: What is this polygon called?
items.e: The star has 5 points, but count the sides: 2 sides for each point, 5 × 2 = 10. It is a decagon.

items.q: A polygon has 8 sides. What is it called?
items.e: 8 sides make an octagon. A stop sign is an octagon.

items.q: How many sides does a decagon have?
items.e: Deca means 10, so a decagon has 10 sides.

items.q: How many sides does a heptagon have?
items.e: A heptagon has 7 sides. Hexagon is 6, heptagon is 7, octagon is 8.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Is this polygon regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: All 5 sides are equal and all 5 angles are equal, so it is a regular pentagon.

items.q: Which polygon is regular?
items.e: A has 6 equal sides and 6 equal angles. The rhombus has unequal angles, the rectangle has unequal sides, and the kite has neither.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Is this polygon regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: The sides are different lengths, and 2 angles are right angles while the others are wider. It is an irregular pentagon.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Is this polygon regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: All 6 sides are equal, but the angles are not all the same size, so the hexagon is irregular.

items.q: A rectangle that is not a square has 4 right angles. Is it regular?
c: No, its sides are not all equal
No, it has no right angles
Yes, all its angles are equal
items.e: Its angles are equal, but the long sides and short sides are different. A regular polygon needs equal sides too.

items.q: Which polygon is irregular?
items.e: C is a rhombus. Its sides are equal, but its angles are not. The other three are regular.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: Two sides are short and two are long, and the angles are different sizes, so it is irregular.

items.q: What do we call a regular quadrilateral?
items.e: A square has 4 equal sides and 4 equal angles (right angles). It is the only regular quadrilateral.

items.q: A regular polygon has …
c: all sides equal and all angles equal
items.e: A polygon is regular only when all its sides are equal AND all its angles are equal.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: All 4 angles are right angles, but the long sides and the short sides are different. The rectangle is irregular.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: The top and bottom are different lengths, and the angles at the top are wider than at the bottom. The trapezoid is irregular.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Is this polygon regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: The 3 sides are different lengths and only one angle is a right angle, so the triangle is irregular.

items.q: A rhombus that is not a square has 4 equal sides. Is it regular?
c: Yes, its sides are all equal
No, its angles are not all equal
items.e: Its sides are equal, but 2 angles are wide and 2 are narrow. A regular polygon needs equal angles too.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: All 6 sides are equal and all 6 angles are equal, so it is a regular hexagon.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Is this polygon regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: All 4 sides are equal and all 4 angles are right angles, so the square is a regular quadrilateral.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: The 4 sides are equal, but 2 angles are narrow and 2 are wide. Equal sides alone do not make a polygon regular. This rhombus is irregular.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Is this polygon regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: All 6 angles are equal, but 3 sides are long and 3 are short, so the hexagon is irregular.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Is this polygon regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: All 8 sides are equal and all 8 angles are equal, so it is a regular octagon.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: All 3 sides are equal and all 3 angles are equal, so it is a regular triangle.

items.q: Same marks mean equal sides or equal angles. Regular or irregular?
c: Irregular: sides and angles not equal
items.e: All 8 angles are equal, but 4 sides are long and 4 are short, so the octagon is irregular.

items.q: Where does this shape go in the Venn diagram?
items.e: It is a regular hexagon. It has 6 sides, not 4. It fits “Regular” but not “4 sides”, so it goes in A.

items.q: Where does this shape go in the Venn diagram?
items.e: It is a regular pentagon: equal sides and equal angles. It fits both “All sides equal” and “All angles equal”, so it goes in the middle, B.

items.q: Which shape goes in the middle of a Venn diagram with “Triangle” and “Regular”?
items.e: B is a triangle with 3 equal sides and 3 equal angles. The other triangles are irregular, and the square is not a triangle.

items.q: Where does this shape go in the Venn diagram?
items.e: It is a rectangle: 4 sides, but the sides are not all equal, so it is not regular. It fits “4 sides” but not “Regular”, so it goes in C.

items.q: Where does this shape go in the Venn diagram?
items.e: It is a turned square. It has 4 right angles and it is regular. It fits both “Has a right angle” and “Regular”, so it goes in the middle, B.

items.q: Which shape fits “All sides equal” but NOT “All angles equal”?
items.e: A is a rhombus. Its sides are equal, but its angles are not.

items.q: Which shape goes outside both circles of a Venn diagram with “Regular” and “Has a right angle”?
items.e: B is a parallelogram: it has no right angle and it is not regular. The square is in both circles, the hexagon is regular, and the rectangle has right angles.

items.q: Where does this shape go in the Venn diagram?
items.e: It is a rhombus: equal sides, but 2 wide and 2 narrow angles. It fits “All sides equal” but not “All angles equal”, so it goes in A.

items.q: Where does this shape go in the Venn diagram?
items.e: It is a triangle with sides of different lengths: not regular and not 4 sides. It fits neither “Regular” nor “4 sides”, so it goes outside both circles, D.

items.q: Ryan puts these shapes in a group called “Regular”: a square, a regular triangle, a rhombus and a regular hexagon. Which shape is in the wrong group?
items.e: A rhombus that is not a square has equal sides but unequal angles, so it is irregular.

items.q: Where does this shape go in the Venn diagram?
items.e: It is a regular triangle. Its angles are equal, and none is a right angle. It fits “Regular” but not “Has a right angle”, so it goes in C.

items.q: Where does this shape go in the Venn diagram?
items.e: It has right angles, but its sides are different lengths, so it is not regular. It fits “Has a right angle” but not “Regular”, so it goes in A.

items.q: Where does this shape go in the Venn diagram?
items.e: It is a square: 4 equal sides and 4 equal angles. It fits both “Regular” and “4 sides”, so it goes in the middle, B.

items.q: A Venn diagram has the circles “Has a right angle” and “Regular”. Where does a rectangle that is not a square go?
items.e: A rectangle has 4 right angles, but its sides are not all equal, so it is not regular. It goes in “Has a right angle” only.

items.q: A Venn diagram has the circles “All sides equal” and “All angles equal”. What kind of polygons go in the middle?
items.e: In the middle, a polygon has all sides equal AND all angles equal. That is what a regular polygon is.

items.q: Where does this shape go in the Venn diagram?
items.e: It is a kite shape. Its sides are not all equal and its angles are not all equal. It fits neither “All sides equal” nor “All angles equal”, so it goes outside both circles, D.

items.q: Mei sorts shapes into “Quadrilaterals” and “Not quadrilaterals”. Which shape is NOT a quadrilateral?
items.e: A quadrilateral has 4 sides. A trapezoid, a rhombus and a square each have 4 sides. A hexagon has 6.

items.q: Which shape goes in the middle of a Venn diagram with the circles “Regular” and “4 sides”?
items.e: D is a square: it has 4 sides and it is regular. The rhombus and the rectangle are irregular, and the pentagon has 5 sides.

items.q: Where does this shape go in the Venn diagram?
items.e: Its 8 angles are equal, but it has long sides and short sides. It fits “All angles equal” but not “All sides equal”, so it goes in C.

items.q: Where does this shape go in the Venn diagram?
items.e: It is a parallelogram with no right angles. Its sides and angles are not all equal. It fits neither “Has a right angle” nor “Regular”, so it goes outside both circles, D.

sets.title: Polygons in real life: word problems

items.q: Ji-woo flies a kite at Stanley Park. It has 4 straight sides: 2 short sides of 30 cm and 2 long sides of 50 cm. Is the kite a regular polygon?
c: No, its sides are not all equal
Yes, it has 2 pairs of equal sides
items.e: A regular polygon has all sides equal. The kite has 30 cm and 50 cm sides, so it is irregular.

items.q: How many green triangle blocks cover one yellow hexagon block?
items.e: 6 triangles fit around the centre of the hexagon. (3 is the number of blue rhombuses, and 2 is the number of red trapezoids.)

items.q: Which pattern block is a regular polygon?
items.e: The yellow hexagon has 6 equal sides and 6 equal angles. The trapezoid has a long side, and the two rhombuses have unequal angles.

items.q: A school zone sign in BC has this shape. It has 2 right angles at the bottom. What is it?
items.e: It has 5 sides, so it is a pentagon. Its angles are not all equal (2 right angles and 3 wider angles), so it is irregular.

items.q: Simran draws a regular octagon. Each side is 4 cm. What is the distance all the way around?
items.e: A regular octagon has 8 equal sides: 8 × 4 cm = 32 cm.

items.q: A window in Nadia's house in Victoria is a square. Is the window a regular polygon?
c: Yes, 4 equal sides and 4 equal angles
items.e: A square has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles, which are equal angles. It is a regular polygon.

items.q: The red trapezoid pattern block has 3 short sides of the same length and 1 long side. Is it regular?
c: No, its sides are not all equal
items.e: One side is longer than the other three, so not all sides are equal. The trapezoid is irregular.

items.q: Mateo's family builds a garden bed shaped like a regular hexagon in Kelowna. Each side is 2 m long. How many metres of edging go all the way around?
items.e: A regular hexagon has 6 equal sides: 6 × 2 m = 12 m.

items.q: A floor at a Surrey community centre is covered by regular hexagon tiles with no gaps. Which other regular polygon can also cover a floor with no gaps?
items.e: 4 squares fit around a corner with no gaps. Regular pentagons, heptagons and octagons always leave gaps. (Regular triangles work too.)

items.q: Leah makes a sign for the Terry Fox Run. She wants a regular polygon with 3 sides. What should she cut out?
c: a triangle with a right angle
items.e: A regular triangle has 3 equal sides and 3 equal angles. It is also called an equilateral triangle.

items.q: Jasleen finds a metal nut shaped like a regular hexagon. How many equal angles does it have?
items.e: A regular hexagon has 6 vertices, so it has 6 angles, and they are all equal.

items.q: A yield sign is a triangle with 3 equal sides and 3 equal angles. Which word describes it?
items.e: All sides are equal and all angles are equal, so the yield sign is a regular triangle.

items.q: A soccer ball has 12 patches shaped like pentagons. How many sides do the 12 pentagons have in all?
items.e: Each pentagon has 5 sides: 12 × 5 = 60. (72 would be 12 × 6, for hexagons.)
A polygon has only straight sides. The rounded corners are curves, so the rink outline is not a polygon.

items.q: A stop sign has 8 equal sides and 8 equal angles. What shape is it?
items.e: 8 sides make an octagon. The sides and angles are all equal, so it is a regular octagon.

items.q: Sofia draws a polygon with 5 sides. Every side is 3 cm, but the angles are not all equal. What did she draw?
items.e: 5 sides make a pentagon. Equal sides are not enough: the angles must be equal too. It is irregular.

items.q: Ava cuts a round pizza into 8 slices. Is one slice a polygon?
c: No, the crust edge is curved
items.e: A slice has 2 straight cut edges, but the crust edge is curved. A polygon has only straight sides.

items.q: Liam says, “A rectangle is regular because all 4 angles are right angles.” Is he right?
c: No, the sides must be equal too
items.e: A regular polygon needs equal sides AND equal angles. Only a square is a regular rectangle.

items.q: The flag of Canada is a rectangle twice as long as it is tall. Is its outline a regular polygon?
c: No, its sides are not all equal
Yes, all its angles are equal
No, it has no right angles
items.e: The flag has 4 right angles, but the long sides are twice as long as the short sides. Equal angles alone do not make it regular.

items.q: Bees build honeycomb cells shaped like regular hexagons. How many sides does each cell have?
items.e: A hexagon has 6 sides. Each cell is a regular hexagon: 6 equal sides and 6 equal angles.
